verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 22.80
verses.english: Linked Discourses 22.80

verses.pali: 8. Khajjanīyavagga
verses.english: 8. Bitable

verses.pali: Piṇḍolyasutta
verses.english: Beggars

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā kismiñcideva pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paṇāmetvā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kapilavatthuṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
verses.english: Then the Buddha, having dismissed the mendicant Saṅgha for some reason, robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Kapilavatthu for alms.

verses.pali: Kapilavatthusmiṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena mahāvanaṁ tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya.
verses.english: He wandered for alms in Kapilavatthu. After the meal, on his return from almsround, he went to the Great Wood for the day’s meditation,

verses.pali: Mahāvanaṁ ajjhogāhetvā beluvalaṭṭhikāya mūle divāvihāraṁ nisīdi.
verses.english: plunged deep into it, and sat at the root of a young wood-apple tree to meditate.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
verses.english: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

verses.pali: “mayā kho bhikkhusaṅgho pabāḷho.
verses.english: “I have purged the mendicant Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ.
verses.english: But there are mendicants here who are junior, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training.

verses.pali: Tesaṁ mamaṁ apassantānaṁ siyā aññathattaṁ siyā vipariṇāmo.
verses.english: Not seeing me they may change and fall apart.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma vacchassa taruṇassa mātaraṁ apassantassa siyā aññathattaṁ siyā vipariṇāmo;
verses.english: If a young calf doesn’t see its mother it may change and fall apart. …

verses.pali: evameva santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ tesaṁ mamaṁ apassantānaṁ siyā aññathattaṁ siyā vipariṇāmo.
Seyyathāpi nāma bījānaṁ taruṇānaṁ udakaṁ alabhantānaṁ siyā aññathattaṁ siyā vipariṇāmo;
verses.english: Or if young seedlings don’t get water they may change and fall apart.

verses.pali: evameva santettha …pe…
verses.english: In the same way, there are mendicants here who are junior, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training.

verses.pali: tesaṁ mamaṁ alabhantānaṁ dassanāya siyā aññathattaṁ siyā vipariṇāmo.
verses.english: Not seeing me they may change and fall apart.

verses.pali: Yannūnāhaṁ yatheva mayā pubbe bhikkhusaṅgho anuggahito, evameva etarahi anuggaṇheyyaṁ bhikkhusaṅghan”ti.
verses.english: Why don’t I support the mendicant Saṅgha now as I did in the past?”

verses.pali: Atha kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—brahmaloke antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi.
verses.english: Then the divinity Sahampati knew the Buddha’s train of thought. As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the realm of divinity and reappeared in front of the Buddha.

verses.pali: Atha kho brahmā sahampati ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṁ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: He arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and said:

verses.pali: “evametaṁ, bhagavā, evametaṁ, sugata.
verses.english: “That’s so true, Blessed One! That’s so true, Holy One!

verses.pali: Bhagavatā, bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho pabāḷho.
verses.english: The Buddha has purged the mendicant Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ.
verses.english: But there are mendicants who are junior, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training. …

verses.pali: Tesaṁ bhagavantaṁ apassantānaṁ siyā aññathattaṁ siyā vipariṇāmo.
Seyyathāpi nāma vacchassa taruṇassa mātaraṁ apassantassa siyā aññathattaṁ siyā vipariṇāmo;
evameva santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ tesaṁ bhagavantaṁ apassantānaṁ siyā aññathattaṁ siyā vipariṇāmo.
Seyyathāpi nāma bījānaṁ taruṇānaṁ udakaṁ alabhantānaṁ siyā aññathattaṁ siyā vipariṇāmo;
evameva santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ, tesaṁ bhagavantaṁ alabhantānaṁ dassanāya siyā aññathattaṁ siyā vipariṇāmo.
Abhinandatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṁ;
verses.english: May the Buddha be happy with the mendicant Saṅgha!

verses.pali: abhivadatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṁ.
verses.english: May the Buddha welcome the mendicant Saṅgha!

verses.pali: Yatheva bhagavatā pubbe bhikkhusaṅgho anuggahito, evameva etarahi anuggaṇhātu bhikkhusaṅghan”ti.
verses.english: May the Buddha support the mendicant Saṅgha now as he did in the past!”

verses.pali: Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.
verses.english: The Buddha consented with silence.

verses.pali: Atha kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato adhivāsanaṁ viditvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
verses.english: Then the divinity Sahampati, knowing that the Buddha had consented, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena nigrodhārāmo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
verses.english: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to the Banyan Tree Monastery, where he sat on the seat spread out.

verses.pali: Nisajja kho bhagavā tathārūpaṁ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkhāsi yathā te bhikkhū ekadvīhikāya sārajjamānarūpā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkameyyuṁ.
verses.english: Then he used his psychic power to will that the mendicants would come to him timidly, alone or in pairs.

verses.pali: Tepi bhikkhū ekadvīhikāya sārajjamānarūpā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: Those mendicants approached the Buddha timidly, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to them:

verses.pali: “Antamidaṁ, bhikkhave, jīvikānaṁ yadidaṁ piṇḍolyaṁ.
verses.english: “This is the last of lifestyles, mendicants, namely relying on alms.

verses.pali: Abhisāpoyaṁ, bhikkhave, lokasmiṁ piṇḍolo vicarasi pattapāṇīti.
verses.english: The world curses you: ‘You beggar, walking bowl in hand!’

verses.pali: Tañca kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, kulaputtā upenti atthavasikā, atthavasaṁ paṭicca;
verses.english: Yet earnest gentlemen take it up for a good reason.

verses.pali: neva rājābhinītā, na corābhinītā, na iṇaṭṭā, na bhayaṭṭā, na ājīvikāpakatā;
verses.english: Not to escape a summons by a king or a summons for a bandit, or because you were in debt or in fear, or in order to make a living.

verses.pali: api ca kho otiṇṇāmha jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi dukkhotiṇṇā dukkhaparetā
verses.english: But because they’re swamped by rebirth, old age, and death; by sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They’re swamped by suffering, mired in suffering.

verses.pali: appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethāti.
verses.english: And they think, ‘Hopefully I can make an end to this entire mass of suffering.’

verses.pali: Evaṁ pabbajito cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, kulaputto.
verses.english: That’s how this gentleman has gone forth.

verses.pali: So ca hoti abhijjhālu kāmesu tibbasārāgo byāpannacitto paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo muṭṭhassati asampajāno asamāhito vibbhantacitto pākatindriyo.
verses.english: Yet they covet sensual pleasures; they’re infatuated, full of ill will and malicious intent. They are unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying mind and undisciplined faculties.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, chavālātaṁ ubhatopadittaṁ majjhe gūthagataṁ, neva gāme kaṭṭhatthaṁ pharati, nāraññe kaṭṭhatthaṁ pharati.
verses.english: Suppose there was a firebrand for lighting a funeral pyre, burning at both ends, and smeared with dung in the middle. It couldn’t be used as timber either in the village or the wilderness.

verses.pali: Tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi gihibhogā ca parihīno, sāmaññatthañca na paripūreti.
verses.english: I say that individual is just like this. They’ve missed out on the pleasures of the lay life, and haven’t fulfilled the goal of the ascetic life.

verses.pali: Tayome, bhikkhave, akusalavitakkā—
verses.english: There are these three unskillful thoughts.

verses.pali: kāmavitakko, byāpādavitakko, vihiṁsāvitakko.
verses.english: Sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts.

verses.pali: Ime ca bhikkhave, tayo akusalavitakkā kva aparisesā nirujjhanti?
verses.english: And where do these three unskillful thoughts cease without remainder?

verses.pali: Catūsu vā satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacittassa viharato animittaṁ vā samādhiṁ bhāvayato.
verses.english: In those who meditate with their mind firmly established in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation; or who develop signless immersion.

verses.pali: Yāvañcidaṁ, bhikkhave, alameva animitto samādhi bhāvetuṁ.
verses.english: This is quite enough motivation to develop signless immersion.

verses.pali: Animitto, bhikkhave, samādhi bhāvito bahulīkato mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso.
verses.english: When signless immersion is developed and cultivated it is very fruitful and beneficial.

verses.pali: Dvemā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyo—
verses.english: There are these two views.

verses.pali: bhavadiṭṭhi ca vibhavadiṭṭhi ca.
verses.english: Views favoring existence and views favoring nonexistence.

verses.pali: Tatra kho, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
verses.english: A learned noble disciple reflects on this:

verses.pali: ‘atthi nu kho taṁ kiñci lokasmiṁ yamahaṁ upādiyamāno na vajjavā assan’ti?
verses.english: ‘Is there anything in the world that I could grasp without fault?’

verses.pali: So evaṁ pajānāti:
verses.english: They understand:

verses.pali: ‘natthi nu kho taṁ kiñci lokasmiṁ yamahaṁ upādiyamāno na vajjavā assaṁ.
verses.english: ‘There’s nothing in the world that I could grasp without fault.

verses.pali: Ahañhi rūpaññeva upādiyamāno upādiyeyyaṁ vedanaññeva …
verses.english: For in grasping I would grasp only at form, feeling,

verses.pali: saññaññeva …
verses.english: perception,

verses.pali: saṅkhāreyeva viññāṇaññeva upādiyamāno upādiyeyyaṁ.
verses.english: choices, or consciousness.

verses.pali: Tassa me assa upādānapaccayā bhavo;
verses.english: That grasping of mine would be a condition for continued existence.

verses.pali: bhavapaccayā jāti;
verses.english: Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.

verses.pali: jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhaveyyuṁ.
verses.english: Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.

verses.pali: Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo assā’ti.
verses.english: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.’

verses.pali: Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
verses.english: What do you think, mendicants?

verses.pali: rūpaṁ niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: Is form permanent or impermanent?”

verses.pali: “Aniccaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Impermanent, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”

verses.pali: “Dukkhaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Suffering, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:

verses.pali: ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’”ti?
verses.english: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

verses.pali: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “No, sir.”

verses.pali: “Vedanā …
verses.english: “Is feeling …

verses.pali: saññā …
verses.english: perception …

verses.pali: saṅkhārā …
verses.english: choices …

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ …pe…
verses.english: consciousness permanent or impermanent?” …

verses.pali: tasmātiha, bhikkhave,
verses.english: “So you should truly see …

verses.pali: evaṁ passaṁ …
verses.english: Seeing this …

verses.pali: nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti.
verses.english: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

verses.pali: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
